primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: HSD3B2 converts Δ5 steroids to Δ4 steroids in adrenal cortex and gonads: pregnenolone to progesterone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone to 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and DHEA to androstenedione. Deficiency reduces glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, and gonadal sex-steroid synthesis and raises Δ5 precursors.
vignette: A 10-day-old infant with a 46,XY karyotype is evaluated for poor feeding, dehydration, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Examination shows severe hypospadias. Laboratory testing shows low cortisol and aldosterone with markedly elevated pregnenolone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone, and DHEA, while progesterone, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, androstenedione, and testosterone are low.
lead: Deficiency of which of the following enzymatic reactions best explains this steroid profile?
correct: Conversion of pregnenolone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone, and DHEA to their corresponding Δ4 steroids
distractors: Conversion of progesterone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone to 11-deoxycorticosterone and 11-deoxycortisol
Conversion of 17-hydroxypregnenolone to DHEA and 17-hydroxyprogesterone to androstenedione
Conversion of 11-deoxycorticosterone and 11-deoxycortisol to corticosterone and cortisol
Conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone in androgen-responsive tissues
distractor_notes: This describes 21-hydroxylase activity; its deficiency characteristically raises 17-hydroxyprogesterone rather than producing a generalized Δ5-to-Δ4 conversion defect.
This describes 17,20-lyase activity of CYP17A1. The stem instead shows accumulation of multiple Δ5 steroids with low corresponding Δ4 products.
This describes 11β-hydroxylase activity. Deficiency would raise 11-deoxysteroids and commonly produce mineralocorticoid hypertension rather than this pattern.
5α-reductase acts peripherally on testosterone and does not cause combined adrenal salt wasting with accumulation of pregnenolone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone, and DHEA.
key_expl: HSD3B2 is expressed in adrenal cortex and gonads and is required for the Δ5-to-Δ4 conversion of several steroid intermediates. It converts pregnenolone to progesterone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone to 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and DHEA to androstenedione. Severe deficiency therefore produces low cortisol and aldosterone, impaired androgen synthesis in 46,XY infants, salt wasting, and accumulation of Δ5 precursors.
objective: Recognize HSD3B2 deficiency from accumulation of Δ5 steroids and identify the shared Δ5-to-Δ4 steroid conversion catalyzed by 3β-HSD2.
